case_title: Birender Poddar v. State of Bihar
evidence_type: Circumstantial; medical (post-mortem by PW-9); oral evidence of related witnesses (PWs 5, 6, 7, 8); documentary (letter, Ext. 1)
aggravating_circumstances: Consistent ill-treatment and torture of the victim; beating and injury marks; deep incised neck and abdominal injuries sufficient to cause death
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302/34, life imprisonment; convicted under IPC s.498-A, two years rigorous imprisonment, concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentences affirmed
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 read with s.34; cruelty under IPC s.498-A
neutral_facts: The victim, a married woman, died within the matrimonial home. The prosecution case rested entirely on circumstantial evidence. Several witnesses who were relatives of the victim, including the victim's father, a cousin and a brother, deposed that the victim had been subjected to consistent ill-treatment at the matrimonial home. According to their evidence, the accused was having an illicit relationship with a sister-in-law, and when the victim complained about this, the victim was tortured. The victim had written letters to her father complaining of this ill-treatment; one such letter was placed on record as an exhibit. Witnesses also spoke of beating and visible injury marks on the victim. The post-mortem was conducted by a doctor, who recorded two incised injuries on the body: a deep incised wound on the front of the neck, at the level of the thyroid cartilage, which had completely cut the trachea and cut major neck veins, and a second incised wound on the upper right side of the abdomen through which the small intestine protruded. The doctor's evidence was that these injuries were sufficient to cause death. The body showed some petrification because of the time gap between death and the post-mortem examination. The victim's identity was confirmed by the father, a cousin and a brother, and the hospital released the body to the father, who had it cremated. The defence case was that the victim had been suffering from jaundice and died a natural death. The only witness called in support was not shown to be a medical practitioner and stated only that the victim had been referred for treatment to Patna on 02.09.1993; no record of jaundice treatment was produced.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from deep incised neck injury (trachea completely cut, neck veins cut) and incised abdominal injury; additional beating and injury marks
motive: alleged: Accused's illicit relationship with his brother's wife; the victim complained of it and was tortured for complaining
key_evidence_accepted: Evidence of PWs 5, 6, 7 and 8 (relatives) on ill-treatment and illicit relationship; letter Ext. 1 written by victim to PW-8; post-mortem testimony of PW-9 and report Ext. 4; identification of body by PWs 5, 7 and 8
witness_credibility: Related witnesses PWs 5-8 found cogent and reliable after careful scrutiny; relatives not discarded merely for being related; defence witness PW-12 not shown to be a medical practitioner and did not depose to jaundice
custody_duration: Not stated (counsel referred only to 'all these years'; no duration given)
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given (Sessions Trial No. 380 of 1994); High Court: 18.7.2002; Supreme Court: 16 May 2011
legal_representation: Accused (appellant): Manu Shanker Mishra, Rituraj Choudhary, Mayur Chaturvedi, C.D. Singh. State: Gopal Singh, Chandan Kumar
investigation_status: Trial completed (Sessions Trial No. 380 of 1994); investigation details not described
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302/34 (life) and s.498-A (two years RI, concurrent). High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentences affirmed. Supreme Court: SLP of three co-petitioners dismissed for non-surrender; leave granted to appellant; appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: No contradiction in material part of the prosecution case; defence of jaundice not proved; hostile witnesses did not support defence; concurrent findings of both courts correct
defence_argument: No direct evidence; substantial contradiction on identification of dead body and between medical and oral evidence; PWs 1-3 hostile; PWs 5-8 interested relatives; natural death from jaundice; should be set free given long custody
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence must form a complete chain unmistakably pointing to guilt; any hypothesis consistent with innocence defeats conviction; interested witnesses' evidence not discarded merely for being related but must be carefully scrutinised
precedent_relied_upon: Hanumant Govind Nargundkar v. State of MP (1952 SCR 1091 = AIR 1952 SC 343); Bhagat Ram v. State of Punjab (AIR 1954 SC 621); Eradu v. State of Hyderabad (AIR 1956 SC 316). Referred: Namdeo v. State of Maharashtra (2007) 14 SCC 150; State of Maharashtra v. Ahmed Shaikh Babajan (2009) 14 SCC 267. Held inapplicable: Rajendra v. State of UP (2009) 13 SCC 480
